visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a close-up shot of a giant, stylized female lantern figure known as 'Nuwa.' The figure has vibrant pink hair, large eyes, and is wearing a gold and pink mosaic-patterned outfit. A golden, halo-like sun ornament is positioned behind her head. The background is a bright, overcast sky. (2) A male host with dark hair, wearing a black blazer over a black shirt, appears in a medium shot. He stands in front of a dark studio background with digital screen elements displaying news-related graphics. He uses active hand gestures as he speaks directly to the camera. (3) The scene switches to night footage from the lantern festival in Taichung Central Park. Various lanterns are shown, including a giant dragon-snake hybrid lantern and the moving Nuwa lantern. Colorful neon lights and geometric structures are visible in the background. (4) Further shots show different lantern displays, including traditional-style paper figures arranged in a group, which have a more somber or 'ghostly' appearance. The lighting is low-key, focused on the lanterns themselves against the night sky. (5) The video returns to the host in the studio for the conclusion. He looks into the lens with a friendly expression, continuing his hand-gestured explanation before the screen fades to black.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to report on the public's polarized reaction to the 'Nuwa' theme lantern at the Taichung Lantern Festival. It uses a combination of news clips and host commentary to highlight both the technical innovation of the moving lantern and the aesthetic controversy, eventually inviting audience engagement by asking for their personal opinions.
